text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- FDP portrays itself as party of reform and as a reliable party at meeting in Stuttgart. Calls for elimination of solidarity tax by the turn of the century.
- Interior Minister Manfred Kanther wants to cut sick day levels of civil servants, which he says are higher than in private industry.
- Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann says introduction of tolls on German motorways only possible after annual vehicle taxes are eliminated.
- Disgraced Frankfurt building tycoon Juergen Schneider charged with fraud, may spend 15 years if convicted.
HANDELSBLATT
- FDP wants new formula for pension system, plans to put new pressure for pension system reform. Party leaders call for quick results.
- Schneider charged with fraud.
- DIW institute says eastern Germany cause for concern, unemployment will keep rising into next year and will hit 4.5 million
- Former Russian security adviser Alexander Lebed to visit Germany for five days starting January 14.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- FDP insists on cutting solidarity tax by end of century.
- Wissmann says motorway toll possible after the year 2000
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt calls for German retailers to be allowed to open shops on Sundays.
DIE WELT
- FDP calls for abolition of solidarity tax by year 2000.
- Juergen Schneider faces 15 years in jail.
- German business leaders confident about economic developments. More than half rate the current economic conditions as "very good" or "mostly good" -- up from 42 percent six months ago.
